newsitem.title: USA: SWIMMING-OLYMPIANS RULE AT U.S. NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-OLYMPIANS RULE AT U.S. NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: The first six of eight events at the U.S. National Swimming Championships Thursday night were won by 1996 U.S. Olympians.
"It makes a statement that we still have swimmers in shape, swimming well and excited about the future," said U.S. national team director Dennis Pursley.
Five-time Olympic gold medalist Jenny Thompson and schoolgirl Amanda Beard won their first major races since the Olympic Games in Atlanta last summer.
Thompson, 23-year-old former world record holder and current American record holder in the 100-metre freestyle, won the event in 55.47 seconds.
"I'm ready to get excited about swimming again," Thompson said. "I felt sluggish in the water, so to do this well is a good sign that I'm back."
Thompson has six career Olympic gold medals, including three at the Atlanta Olympics -- second most by an American female swimmer.
Beard, 15, won the 200-metre breaststroke in 2 minutes, 30.73 seconds, just one month after having a cyst removed from her right wrist.
"I wasn't able to train for about a month after the surgery so this was a good test," Beard said.
At the Olympics, Beard took silver in both the 100 and 200 breaststroke events. She won a gold medal on the 400-metre medley relay.

Other 1996 Olympians winning here were Brad Bridgewater in the 200-metre backstroke in 2:00.74, Kurt Grote in the 200 breaststroke in 2:14.39, Beth Botsford in the 200 backstroke in 2:12.49 and Bradley Schumacher in the 100 freestyle in 51.33.
Thursday was the second of five days of competition at the first major meet since the Summer Olympic Games in Atlanta.
